result.topic_en: Euler determines the quadratic residues for the composite divisors 3(2p+1) and (2p+1)(2q+1), with the example 35, and then begins Chapter 15 on the divisors of numbers of the form xx+yy.
result.transcription:
Tractatus de numerorum doctrina Cap. 15. 69
De divisore $3(2p+1)=d$.
533. Multitudo numerorum hoc divisore minorum et ad eum primorum est $=2.2p=4p$, inter quos duo ad minimum sunt, quorum quadrata idem residuum relinquunt, scilicet $a^2$ et $(d-a)^2$, unde numerus diversorum residuorum major quam $2p$ esse nequit.
534. Praeterea vero cum $a$ per 3 non sit divisibile, vel $2p+1-2a$, vel $2(2p+1)-2a$ per 3 erit divisibile, sit quotus $=m$, et quadratum numeri $3m+a$ idem relinquet residuum, ergo vel $2p+1-a$, vel $2(2p+1)-a$, indeque praeterea vel $2(2p+1)+a$, vel $2p+1+a$ idem quoque residuum relinquet.
535. Hoc modo cum semper quaterna quadrata idem dent residuum, numerus residuorum diversorum erit tantum $=p$, ideoque idem ac pro divisore $2p+1$. In residuis autem nequit esse ullus numerus formae $3n-1$, cum nullum quadratum, tali numero minutum, per 3, neque ergo per $3(2p+1)$ dividi queat.
536. Omnia ergo residua divisoris $3(2p+1)$ erunt numeri formae $3n+1$, et si residua divisoris $2p+1$ sint $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma$, etc. quodlibet vel ipsum, vel numero $2p+1$, vel $2(2p+1)$ auctum, quo prodeat numerus formae $3n+1$, erit residuum divisoris $3(2p+1)$.
Pro divisore $(2p+1)(2q+1)=d$.
537. Sint pro divisore $2p+1$ residua $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. numero $=p$, et pro divisore $2q+1$ residua $1, \pi, \varrho, \sigma, \tau$, etc. numero $=q$, ac numeri utrique ordini communes erunt residua divisoris $d=(2p+1)(2q+1)$.
538. At ad priorem ordinem pertinere censendus est numerus $m(2p+1)+\alpha$, ubi $m$ ita potest definiri, ut fiat aequalis vel $n(2q+1)+1$, vel $n(2q+1)+\pi$, etc., sicque ex quovis residuo divisoris $2p+1$ producuntur $q$ residua divisoris $2q+1$, sicque omnino $pq$ residua diversa pro divisore $(2p+1)(2q+1)$ obtinentur.
539. Sit hujusmodi divisor compositus $5.7=35$, et cum sint residua pro divisore 5 haec duo $1, 4$, et pro 7 haec tria $1, 2, 4$; ergo pro divisore 35 residua erunt $7n+1$, $7n+2$, $7n+4$, quae scilicet vel in forma $5m+1$, vel $5m+4$ continentur. Erunt ergo haec residua numero sex: $1, 29; 9, 16; 4, 11$.
540. Cum pro divisore $(2p+1)(2q+1)$ tantum dentur $pq$ residua diversa, quaterna quadrata idem praebebunt residuum, quorum unum si sit $=aa$, reliquorum trium radices erunt:
$(2p+1)(2q+1)-a, \quad m(2p+1)-a, \quad n(2p+1)+a$,
sumendis numeris $m$ et $n$ ita, ut $m(2p+1)-2a$ et $n(2p+1)+2a$ dividi queant per $2q+1$, quod ob $2p+1$ et $2q+1$ primos inter se, semper fieri potest, ut $m$ et $n$ sint minores quam $2q+1$.
Caput XV.
De divisoribus numerorum formae $xx+yy$.
541. Hinc primo excludo casus, quibus numeri $x$ et $y$ habent communem divisorem; si enim maximus communis divisor esset $=\varphi$ et $x=p\varphi$ et $y=q\varphi$, ut $p$ et $q$ forent primi inter se, haberetur $xx+yy=(pp+qq)\varphi\varphi$, et inventio divisorum reduceretur ad formam $pp+qq$.

methods.what: Upper bound for the number of distinct quadratic residues modulo 3(2p+1), since a² and (d−a)² agree
methods.quote: Multitudo numerorum hoc divisore minorum et ad eum primorum est $=2.2p=4p$, inter quos duo ad minimum sunt, quorum quadrata idem residuum relinquunt, scilicet $a^2$ et $(d-a)^2$, unde numerus diversorum residuorum major quam $2p$ esse nequit.

methods.what: Four squares share each residue modulo 3(2p+1), so there are p distinct quadratic residues
methods.quote: Hoc modo cum semper quaterna quadrata idem dent residuum, numerus residuorum diversorum erit tantum $=p$, ideoque idem ac pro divisore $2p+1$.

methods.what: Quadratic residues modulo 3(2p+1) are ≡1 (mod 3) and are obtained by lifting the residues mod 2p+1
methods.quote: Omnia ergo residua divisoris $3(2p+1)$ erunt numeri formae $3n+1$

methods.what: Residues modulo a product of coprime odd moduli are the numbers common to both residue classes (CRT-type combination), giving pq residues
methods.quote: sicque omnino $pq$ residua diversa pro divisore $(2p+1)(2q+1)$ obtinentur.

methods.what: Worked example: the quadratic residues mod 35
methods.quote: Erunt ergo haec residua numero sex: $1, 29; 9, 16; 4, 11$.

methods.what: The four square roots of a residue aa modulo (2p+1)(2q+1)
Reduction of xx+yy with a common divisor to the coprime case
methods.quote: haberetur $xx+yy=(pp+qq)\varphi\varphi$, et inventio divisorum reduceretur ad formam $pp+qq$.

items.quote: In residuis autem nequit esse ullus numerus formae $3n-1$, cum nullum quadratum, tali numero minutum, per 3, neque ergo per $3(2p+1)$ dividi queat.
items.english: But among the residues there cannot be any number of the form 3n−1, since no square diminished by such a number can be divided by 3, nor therefore by 3(2p+1).

items.quote: quod ob $2p+1$ et $2q+1$ primos inter se, semper fieri potest, ut $m$ et $n$ sint minores quam $2q+1$.
items.english: which, because 2p+1 and 2q+1 are coprime, can always be done so that m and n are less than 2q+1.

items.quote: Hinc primo excludo casus, quibus numeri $x$ et $y$ habent communem divisorem
items.english: Here I first exclude the cases in which the numbers x and y have a common divisor
